Actor.description: Who did what an event says.

id.description:
The account's or agent session's id; for an external actor, its id
at the source.

login.description:
Their login as people read it, when they have one. An external
one's is what the source said, untrusted.

oneOf.description: A person's Arugula account.
An agent, acting for its owner.
Someone at a third party (a GitHub login), not known to Arugula.
A kind this side doesn't know yet.

AgentSessionWork.description: An agent session on this machine's workspace that hasn't ended.

actions.description:
What people asked of the session that the box hasn't done yet,
oldest first: listed on every pull until a report names them done
([`SessionDetail::actions`]).

asker.description: The account it runs as: whose mention started it.

branch.description: The one ref it may push: `arugula/<8 hex of the id>-<slug>`.

finish.description:
The workspace's finish step (M261), if its spec has one: what the
box runs after each turn, before it pushes.

grant.description:
The project's standing grant, on every pull while it has a live one
that gives `runs.instruct` (aru-115, as amended): the box checks it
against what it pinned before it takes the session or starts a turn
(`arugula_e2e::project_grant::check`), and keeps the last one that
checked out, for the revokes that come with every pull
([`Work::revokes`]). With none, the box starts nothing new; a turn
under way finishes.

harness.description:
The agent it runs ([`HARNESSES`]): `claude` unless it says (M264,
a Try 3's sibling or a review). A box without the one asked for
runs `claude`, and its first report says which it ran
([`SessionDetail::harness`]).

model.description:
The model its agent uses (Arugula #215), one of [`MODELS`]: the
one its ask named ("use sonnet"), else its project's setting. `None`:
the strongest, which the box picks ([`DEFAULT_MODEL`] for Claude
Code, Codex's own choice for Codex). The box reports the one it runs
on ([`SessionDetail::model`]).

n.description: The machine's latest report's number: its next report is `n + 1`.

park.description:
Parked (Arugula #215): `done`, with no prompt listed, for at least
[`SESSION_PARK_MS`]. The box closes its agent block, keeping its
user, checkout and conversation; once it lists prompts again the
box opens a block on them, loading the conversation. The platform
lists a parked one's prompts only when the box has a running slot
for it ([`MAX_SESSIONS_PER_BOX`]).

passkey_log.description:
A v2 grant's granter's passkey log, as the platform read it from the
hub (DK6, as [`WorkItem::passkey_log`]), while the session may be
about to start a turn: the machine takes only its removals. `None`:
it goes by what it pinned.

prompts.description: Its queued prompts, oldest first: what the next turn starts with.

repo.description: The linked repo it works in (`owner/name`), if any.

review.description:
A review (M264, `@codex review`): read-only. The box runs no finish
step and pushes nothing, and its turn's report carries the agent's
reply ([`SessionDetail::reply`]), which the platform posts in the
thread.

state.description:
Its state as the machine sees it: `queued`, `working`,
`needs_input` or `done` (an `unresponsive` one is listed in the
state it was in).

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) the machine is.

AnsweredAsk.description: An ask that was answered, kept in the row's history.

kind.description:
An agent's card on the row's issue (Arugula #1469): `todo` (its
`question` is what it asked to be done, its `answer` Done or
Can't) or `approval` (Approve or Deny). None: a board ask.

note.description: A to-do's note, as its record keeps it, for its person alone.

at.description: v3: the statement's time, as chant writes one (`--at`).

by.description: v1: the signing device's id. Empty in v2, which no device signs.

chant.description: v3: the chant gate it approves, as the deploy's plan box read it.

sig.description:
v1: Ed25519 signature by `by` over [`Approval::body`], hex. Empty in
v2, whose passkey assertion is its signature.

v.description:
Its format, [`V1`], [`V2`] or [`V3`]: absent is v1 (every approval
from before DK4).

oneOf.description: Its bytes (standard base64) and its digest (`sha256:<hex>`).
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

Ask.description:
A question on a row that a person answers on the board (Arugula #367):
asked by a person or an agent, or raised by the board itself from the
state of the row's items (`raised`, never stored, and with no answer).

asked_by.description:
Who asked, as a name: a person, or an agent and its machine. Empty
for a raised ask.

can_answer.description: The reader may answer it: the person it names, or an owner or editor.

mine.description: It is for the reader (a raised ask is for whoever reads the row).

raised.description:
The board raised it, from its items' state, and it clears with its
cause: nobody answers it.

who.description: The account it is for; empty for a raised ask.

who_name.description: Who it is for, as the reader's page names them.

Assertion.description:
A passkey's assertion, as the page got it from
`navigator.credentials.get`: each base64url.

Asset.description:
One picture of a Doc, without its bytes: the shape a machine Doc's
state gives (`DocState.assets`).

rev.description:
Changes whenever the name is written with other bytes: clients cache
a picture by `name/rev`.

oneOf.description: The work itself: a PR, an agent block or a run. It moves the lane.
Evidence that the work is done: a run or a link.

block.description: A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it.

live.description:
The item's state now, when the reader may see it: an item they can't
read says nothing, as an unreadable row does.

released.description:
A block that a newer agent took the row from (`take`): it is an
earlier agent whatever it reports, and holds no claim.

BlockState.description:
What a daemon says of one of its own agent blocks, and all it says
(aru-116's second ruling): the state word, the branch, the short HEAD,
whether it is pushed, how many files are uncommitted and the diffstat.
No message text, no file names, no prompts: the type has no field that
could carry them. This is the view, read leniently by a daemon; control
refuses a body with another field through [`BlockStateReport`].

title.description:
The name its starter or its person gave the block: a board's chip
for it. Never the first words of a prompt.

BlockWord.description: What an agent block is doing (aru-116's second ruling).

closed_at.description: When it was closed; absent while it is open.

closed_by.description:
The account that closed it; empty once that account is deleted. When
an agent closed it, the account it acted for.

closed_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent closed it, if one did.

created_by.description:
The account that made it; empty once that account is deleted. When an
agent made it, the account it acted for.

created_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent made it, if one did.

done_note.description:
What was done, written when the board was closed; kept when it is
opened again. Empty before it was ever closed.

goal.description: What the board is for, in a paragraph; empty means none.

lead.description:
The session that leads the board (#414): a post on the board's thread
reaches it. Absent when no session does.

progress.description: How many of its issues are closed.

source.description:
The tracker's epic it follows, when it was made from one (Plane's,
#483); absent for a board a person made.

BoardDoc.description: One Doc of a board: in its strip, or on one row (a row's [`Row::docs`]).

added_by.description: The account that linked it (the owner, for an agent).

agent.description: The machine whose agent linked it, if one did.

machine_name.description: A machine Doc's machine, by name.

missing.description: A project Doc that was deleted.

BoardGrant.description:
A board's standing grant (Arugula #1415, #1416): what its person approved
on its "Run this board" card. Its lead runs on `lead_machine`; its issue
agents on that machine or `machines`, at most `cap` at once.

lapses_at.description: When it lapses; absent: when the board closes.

machines.description: Every machine its issue agents may use: the lead's first.

mine.description: The reader gave it, so Revoke is theirs.

person.description: The account that gave it, and its name now.

running.description: Its issue agents running now (and tickets not attached yet).

BoardLead.description:
The session that leads a board: the machine it runs on and its name there,
as that machine's daemon matches it (#414).

at.description: When the session took the lead.

machine_name.description: The machine's name now; empty while it can't be told.

pane.description:
The leading session's pane on its machine, the one the lead was taken
from: the page finds the pane by it, not by the name, which a renamed
conversation or a pane without a title doesn't match. Absent for a
lead an older daemon took.

BoardProgress.description:
A board's work, counted: the rows with a primary item (an issue or a
PR; a note row is never counted). `done` is those in the Done lane, and
`proven` those of them with a proof; `review` and `doing` are those in
the Review and Doing lanes.

BoardSource.description:
The epic a board follows: its children are the board's rows, and the
connection made the board, not a person.

connection.description: The connection that made the board, as the project calls it.

key.description: The epic's key in the tracker, such as `ARUGU-10`.

left_out.description:
How many children the board is too full to show, the oldest done
ones first.

started.description:
Whether the epic is started in the tracker (Plane's `started` group),
read from its mirrored item; not whether the board is open.

url.description: Where the epic is in the tracker's web app.

BoardView.description:
A board with its four lanes, in order (`lane_next`, `lane_doing`,
`lane_review`, `lane_done`), each with its rows, and its groups, in
order. The rows of a group are those with [`Row::group`] set to its id; a
row without one comes after the grouped ones.

chain.description:
The longest chain of open rows (`row_…`), first to last; empty when
no row waits on another (#762).

docs.description:
The Docs strip, in order. Empty for a board with none; an old client
ignores it.

grant.description: Its live grant to start agents (Arugula #1416), if it has one.

groups.description: Empty for a board with none; an old client ignores it.

order.description:
Every row (`row_…`) as the board stores them: by group, in the
groups' order, then by position inside each, those with no group
last. A move that names the order it read (`seen`) names a group's
rows from here.

ready.description:
The ready set (Arugula #403): the rows (`row_…`) with an issue or a
PR as their item that are in Next and have no open blocker.

said.description:
What a write did that the board alone doesn't say: a PR attached to
the row of the issue it closes, an item that was there already.

sequence.description:
The rows (`row_…`) that have a [`Row::step`], by step, and inside a
step by what unblocks the most open rows, then by position (#762).

Category.description:
Where an item is in its own life, the same words for every source
(Arugula #405): Plane's state groups, which a native issue's and a GitHub
issue's open and closed map onto. A lane reads it: `completed` and
`canceled` are Done, every other category is not.

ChatAgent.description:
The agent that wrote a message (M197): the machine whose grant it acted
through, and its name now. The message's author is the machine's owner.

session.description:
The session that posted, as its machine called it then (#429): an
agent block's title, or the Claude Code session's name. Display
only; never what a permission rests on.

ChatFile.description:
One attached file, as the reader sees it. `url` is control's, for the
room's readers only (a session cookie, or an agent's token): the same
path with `?download=1` downloads it.

mime.description: What the bytes were sniffed as, never what the upload said.

width.description: An image's size in pixels, when its header gave it.

ChatFileKind.description:
How a file is shown: `Image`, `Video` and `Audio` inline (only types
that are safe to render: never SVG or HTML), anything else as a card
that downloads.

oneOf.description: Control hasn't had the machine's daemon's answer yet (#419).
A session took it (`session`), or the daemon didn't say which.
The session it named wasn't there (`asked`): it went to `session`.
No session took it: it waits in the machine's inbox.

The session (`session`) has it queued, but its hooks aren't
listening to take it (#571).

The session it named (`asked`) is there, but its owner silenced
mentions for it (#579): it waits in the machine's inbox.

The session it named isn't there (`asked`), or is more than one:
no other session got it, and it waits in the inbox. `names` are the
ones there are (#576).
The machine is offline, or didn't answer.

The machine's owner turned agent mentions off on it (`arugulad
sharing agent-mentions off`): it refused the mention and kept
nothing. Final: it isn't sent again when the machine connects.
The machine's agent replied in the thread (`reply`).

Not delivered (#575): an agent's post, in a chain of agents' replies
or past the thread's rate limit. A person's message restarts it.

The session's turn that took it has started (#540): what only the
receiving daemon knows. Like a typing indicator.

That turn has ended (#540). An agent's reply, `answered`, usually
comes first and stays.

The session dropped it (#613): `why` says how. Final, like
`answered`, which it never replaces.

The machine's agents can't read the room (#578): its owner was asked
to let them. Delivered if they do; final if they said never.

ChatMentionStatus.description:
Where a message's `@machine` mention got to (#502), as control knows it:
what the machine's daemon said when it was told, and then whether the
machine's agent answered in the thread.

asked.description: The session the message named that the daemon couldn't find.

for_session.description:
The session the message named on the machine, as `@machine/session`
spells it, or none for the machine itself. With `machine`, what tells
one status line from another: a post can name two sessions of one
machine (#875).

machine_name.description: What the machine was called when it was told.

names.description: With `no_such_session`: the names it could have used (#576).

reply.description: With `answered`: the number of the agent's reply.

session.description: The session it went to, when the daemon said.

ChatMessage.description: A message as the reader sees it.

agent.description:
Written by an agent on the author's machine (M197): shown as
"<name>'s agent on <machine_name>".

also.description: A reply that was also sent to the channel.

author.description:
The author's account, and their name now. Both are empty for a
deleted account.

deleted.description: When it was deleted: its text, quote and pane are gone.

files.description:
Files and images attached (#107), in the order they were chosen.
Empty for a deleted message: its files went with it.

imported.description:
Brought in from a machine's own threads (M124): the name it had
there. Someone with no account here (a tailnet login, an agent) is
shown under the machine's owner, by this name.

mention_status.description:
Where each machine's agent mention in it got to (#502), one per
machine, by name. Empty for a message that mentions none.

mentions.description: The accounts it mentions, and the agents (`machine:<id>`, M198).

parent.description:
A reply (#106): the number of its thread's first message. The
room's list has it only with `also`; the thread has it always.

quote.description: Lines the poster chose from a pane, copied in (decision 1).

reactions.description:
Who reacted with which emoji (#104), the first reaction first.
Empty for a deleted message and for archives brought in.

seq.description:
Its number in the room. Messages brought in from a machine (M124)
keep their old numbers, unless the room already had messages of its
own: then they're numbered 0 and below, before control's.

system.description:
Not something said but something that happened (#119): `author` set
the topic or pinned a message. Drawn dim and centered; never
counted unread, pushed, edited or reacted to.

thread.description: The thread of replies this message starts, once it has any.

via.description:
Posted for the author by a product (M237): a hud box's name, for a
review written there. Shown as "<name> via <via>". [`SYSTEM_VIA`]
with no author: a line the platform wrote (#122), shown apart, as
plain text.

ChatPane.description:
A pane a message names, as the reader sees it: whether its chip opens
for them (they may reach the machine), and the machine's name.

ChatPerson.description: Someone, as the reader sees them.

dnd.description:
They've paused their notifications (do not disturb, #115): a moon
on their avatar. Only that it's on, never until when or why.

ChatReaction.description: One emoji on a message, as the reader sees it.

agents.description:
How many of `count` are agents' (#632); the rest are people's. An
older control leaves it out, and it reads as none.

count.description: All who reacted with it; `who` names the first [`MAX_REACTORS_SHOWN`].

mine.description:
The reader has: a person's own reaction, or for an agent reading,
its own (never the owner's, nor the agent's for the owner).

ChatReactor.description:
Someone who reacted: an account, and the machine's agent if it was
the agent reacting for them.

ChatSystem.description: What a system line tells of (#119).

kind.description:
`topic` (its `text` is the new topic, empty when cleared),
`description` (likewise), `pin` or `unpin`.

target.description: The pinned message's number, for `pin` and `unpin`.

ChatThread.description: The replies to a message, as one reader sees them (#106).

following.description: The reader follows the thread. Always false to an agent.

read.description:
The reader's mark in the thread (a room number), and the replies
after it that aren't theirs (only while they follow), and how many
of those mention them.

repliers.description: Who replied, the newest first, at most [`THREAD_REPLIERS`].

replies.description: Replies not deleted, and when the newest was written (ms).

Decision.description: Approve it once, or deny it.

DeployPlanWork.description:
What a deploy's plan run plans (#1985): the deploy's operation, its
driver and settings. No approval: the plan comes before one, and its
run gets no secret of the environment's, only a GitHub token the
platform mints to push chant's ledger ([`DeployPlanWork::secrets`]).

DeployWork.description:
What a deploy's run applies (M219), for its machine to check: the
deploy's operation (`arugula deploy op v1`) and an owner's approval over
it (v2 since DK4: the approval's bytes, and the passkey assertion over
them that is its signature), with the approver's passkey log as the hub
publishes it (DK3). The machine takes only its removals after the log it
pinned from control, never a key it adds
(`arugula_e2e::deploy::check_apply`, `arugula_e2e::passkey::removed_since`).

approval_id.description:
The approval's id (`apv_`), for the driver to note where it records
it (chant's approve note).

passkey_log.description:
The approver's passkey log, as the platform read it from the hub
when it handed out the work. `None` from a platform from before DK4,
or when the hub didn't answer: the machine goes by what it pinned.

roll_back.description:
For a roll back (M220): the earlier deploy it goes back to, and what
that ran. The plan names it too.

secrets.description:
The names of the secrets its driver gets: their values come only
from [`WORK_SECRETS`], while the run runs.

settings.description:
The environment's driver settings (M220): the plan names them, so
the machine checks them against the approved plan
(`arugula_e2e::drivers::planned`).

Diffstat.description: A `git diff --stat` summary line as numbers: nothing of the files.

Doc.description: A Doc, without its sections: a list's row, and a view's head.

agent.description:
The agent session that made it as itself (aru-115): its `machine`
the session's id (`ses_…`), its name `Agent session <id>`; or the
machine whose agent made it for `author` (Arugula #862), its
`machine` and `machine_name` the machine's.

author.description:
The account that made it (an agent's owner's, for one a machine's
agent made), or "" once it's deleted, or for one an agent session made.

layout.description:
How the Doc is laid out: `doc`, `tabs` or `prototype`. Sent only when
it isn't `doc`: absent, or a name the reader doesn't know, is `doc`,
and an older page ignores it and draws the column.

moved_from.description:
For a team Doc a machine moved here (Arugula #863): the machine and
its Doc's id there. Absent for any other Doc, and from an older
platform.

sections.description: How many sections it has, and how many are written.

DocList.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOCS`]: a project's Docs, the latest changed first.

writer.description: Whether the reader may make one.

DocView.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: a Doc with its sections, in order.

deleter.description:
Whether the reader may delete it: a person who writes in the
project. An older platform sends none; the page then takes `writer`.

link.description:
The Doc's page on the platform's page, which the team opens. An older
platform sends none.

public.description:
The Doc's public link, when it has one (Arugula #871). Left out for
an agent session, which is never given the key.

writer.description: Whether the reader may write it.

DocWrite.description:
`PUT` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: what changes. `title` renames it, `layout` lays it out. With `section`,
that section's body becomes `markdown` (and its heading `heading`, when
given); with no `section` but a `heading`, a section is added at the
end, written when `markdown` is given and pending otherwise.

layout.description:
Sets the layout (`doc`, `tabs` or `prototype`); omitted leaves it as
it is.

oneOf.description: The person pressed stop while it waited in the session's queue.
The session's process ended in the middle of its turn.

Event.description: One event of an account's log.

aaguid.description: The authenticator's AAGUID, 32 hex, [`NO_AAGUID`] when unknown.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the body and proof line, hex.

prev.description: The hash of the event before, or [`ZERO`].

proof.description: On a `by passkey` event, the signer's assertion over [`Event::challenge`].

rp.description:
The RP ID it was made for; for a backfilled event, possibly each of
control's sites, space-separated.

actor.description: Who did it, when anyone did.

at_ms.description: When it happened, as its source says, in ms since the epoch.

data.description:
The type's fields: metadata only, at most [`DATA_MAX_BYTES`]
([`data_check`]). Null when it has none.

key.description:
Its identity for deduplication: a second event with the same key is
dropped (a webhook's delivery id, `issue.closed:iss_…:3`).

recorded_ms.description: When the log took it, in ms since the epoch.

seq.description:
Its place in the log, in commit order: a reader by `seq` misses
none.

source.description:
Who it came from: [`SOURCE_ARUGULA`], [`SOURCE_GITHUB`],
[`SOURCE_PLANE`], or another adapter's name.

subject.description:
What it's about, as a ref Arugula already reads: `iss_…`,
`owner/repo#12`, `run_…`, `dep_…`, `ses_…`, a pane's id, or a room
and thread (`room_…#12`).

type.description:
Its type, a name in the catalog (`issue.closed`), or one this side
doesn't know yet.

v.description: The version of its type's `data`, from 1.

EventScope.description: Where an event belongs: who may see it is decided from here.

project.description: The project's id (`prj_…`), when it's in one.

EventsPage.description:
A read of the log: its events in `seq` order, as stored (metadata
only), and where to read on from.

gone_before.description:
The log no longer keeps the events after `after` numbered below
this: they were older than it keeps them, and are gone. None when it
had them all.

head.description:
The log's newest number when it was read. `next_after` below it:
there's more to read.

next_after.description:
The next read's `after`: past every event this one looked at,
including those it left out (another project's or type's, or one
the agent may not see), so none is read twice.

FinishResult.description: What a turn's finish step did (M261), on the turn's report.

command.description: The command, as the spec has it.

output_tail.description:
The last of what it printed (stdout and stderr, at most 4 KiB):
only when it failed.

FinishStep.description:
A workspace's finish step (M261): a command (`just check`) the box runs
as the session's user, in its checkout, after each turn and before the
push. When it fails the agent gets one more turn to fix it, with its
output; when that fails too, the branch isn't pushed.

timeout_s.description: How long it may run, in seconds ([`FINISH_TIMEOUT_S`] when 0).

Gate.description:
The gate a chant→Fly deploy's plan stopped at, as its plan box read it
from the pending fact chant's run recorded on `chant/lifecycle`.

checkpoint.description: The checkpoint a resuming gate carries its outputs from.

environment.description: The pending fact's environment: a component gate's; an op's has none.

plan.description: chant's plan digest (`jcs1-sha256:…`, or an older run's `sha256:…`).

recorded.description: When it did, as chant wrote it: an approval's time can't be earlier.

run.description: The chant run that recorded the pending fact.

GrantMachine.description:
A machine a [`BoardGrant`] names: its id, and its name now (its id while
it can't be told).

GrantRevoke.description:
The project's grants taken back, by any owner: every grant for the
project under `delegation` made at or before `at`, v1 or v2. It names
no grant, so whoever relays it can't point it at another one; a grant
made after it is a new one.

account.description: [`REVOKE_PASSKEY`]: the revoking owner's account, in the bytes.

by.description: [`REVOKE_DEVICE`]: the signing device. Empty in a passkey's.

delegation.description: The delegation whose grants it takes back.

sig.description: [`REVOKE_DEVICE`]: its signature, hex. Empty in a passkey's.

v.description:
Its format, [`REVOKE_DEVICE`] or [`REVOKE_PASSKEY`]: absent is a
device's (every revoke from before DK6).

Group.description:
A named, ordered section of a board that its author sets: a phase, a
wave, an area. A row belongs to at most one ([`Row::group`]); a group
holds no lane, and a row's lane is the same in any group.

progress.description: Its rows with an issue or a PR, counted as a board's are.

agent.description:
The agent that opened it for its owner; or the agent session that
opened it as itself (aru-115), its `machine` the session's id
(`ses_…`) and its name `Agent session <id>`.

author.description:
The account that opened it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted, or for one an agent session opened.

closed_by.description:
Who closed a closed one (an agent's owner's account), as its latest
`closed` event says: a list's row names them (UI audit #163).

closed_by_agent.description: The agent that closed it for its owner.

IssueEvent.description: An event on an issue's timeline.

actor.description:
The account that did it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted.

IssueGithub.description: Where an issue was exported to on GitHub (M205).

more.description: There are more past the last one (`before` its number).

IssueQuery.description:
`GET /api/projects/{project}/issues`'s query. Each that's given narrows
the list.

before.description: Issues numbered below this: the next page.

labels.description: Labels, comma-separated: issues with every one.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

q.description:
Search words, in the title or the body: each one (`dep*`: a word
starting with `dep`).

Lane.description:
Where a row is, worked out on every read from the live state of its
items and never stored (aru-125). Each is the furthest that applies, in
the order `done`, `review`, `doing`, `next`.

oneOf.description: Nothing is under way, or the row is a note.
An agent block that isn't closed, or a run that is running.

A PR is open, or the issue is open and its PR merged (see
[`Mark::NotFinished`]).
The issue is closed, or the PR merged or closed.

LaneSet.description:
A lane a person set on a row ([`Row::lane_set`]). Deprecated with
[`BOARD_ROW_LANE`]: nothing sets one, and no board sends one.

by.description: The account that moved the row.

LaneView.description:
One of a board's four lanes as a read answers it, with its rows. The wire
and TypeScript still call it a zone (`zones`, `BoardZone`).

LeftQueue.description: A PR's last unmerged exit from its merge queue (Arugula #766).

at.description: When the platform heard it, in milliseconds.

reason.description:
GitHub's `reason` as it came, in upper case: `CHECKS_TIMED_OUT`,
`CHECKS_FAILED`, `MERGE_CONFLICT`, `MANUAL`, `BRANCH_PROTECTIONS`,
`GIT_TREE_INVALID`, `INVALID_MERGE_COMMIT`, `UNKNOWN_REMOVAL_REASON`.
One GitHub adds later is kept as it is.

Live.description:
The item a row points at, as it is now: what the page draws beside the
row's own status, and the label of its link.

assignees.description:
Who an issue or PR is assigned to: a mirrored item's logins, a native
issue's names. A run has none.

category.description: An issue's status category; a PR and a run have none.

closed_by.description:
With `closed_with`, the words of the PR that closed it: `"(#12)" in
the title`, `"Closes #12" in the body`, `the branch feat/12-x`,
`attached to its board row as work`. Absent for a close from before
they were kept.

closed_with.description:
A closed native issue that a merged PR closed: the PR
(`OWNER/NAME#N`), so a wrong close is easy to spot (Arugula #743).

identifier.description: A tracker item's project key (`ARUGU`: the card reads `ARUGU-12`).

kind.description:
`pr` or `issue` (a mirrored one), `native` for a native issue, or
`run`.

labels.description:
The item's labels (#547): a native issue's, a mirrored item's, a
Plane item's. A run has none.

left_queue.description: A PR that left the queue unmerged, and why (`ForgeItem::left_queue`).

provider.description: `plane` for a tracker's item; absent for GitHub, native issues and runs.

queued.description:
A PR in its branch's merge queue now (Arugula #766). A repo with no
queue, a platform from before it and every other kind say false.

queued_since.description: With `queued`: when it entered the queue, in milliseconds.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME` of a mirrored item; absent for a native issue.

state_name.description: A tracker item's own state (`In Progress`).

title.description: A run's: how it started (`manual run`).

url.description: Where a tracker item is, in the tracker.

LiveState.description:
What a pointer to an item, an issue or a run is now, from data control
already has (the forge mirror, the issues and runs tables): a separate fact, never written
over the row's stored `status`.

oneOf.description: A PR or an issue, open.
A PR, open, with checks still running.
A PR, open, with red checks.
A PR closed unmerged, or an issue closed.
A run, running.
A run that failed.
A run that is pending, approved, denied, canceled or expired.

began.description:
When this hub began keeping logs (ms): removals before then are in
no log. Said by the hub, not hashed; `None` when it doesn't say.

Mark.description:
A note on a row that its lane doesn't say, worked out on every read and
never stored (aru-125, decisions 7 to 9).

oneOf.description:
What a build before Arugula #841 said of an open issue whose PR
merged, with none open: read as `NotFinished` with no reason and
`merged`. Current platforms never send it.

The row's issue is marked Not finished (Arugula #841), or it is open
and a PR of the row merged, with none open: a merge doesn't close a
marked ticket. `merged`: a PR of the row merged, and the row is in
Review. `reason` is what is left, and is none when nobody marked it
(a merged PR that only said `part of`). A marked row with nothing
merged keeps the lane its work gives it.

by.description:
Who marked it: a login or name, and for an agent "<person>'s
agent on <machine>" as the board names an agent.

oneOf.description:
The row's item was canceled (a Plane `cancelled` state, a native issue
closed as not planned or as a duplicate): the row is Done and never
proven, whatever merged.

An open PR of the row is stacked on another open PR: it targets that
PR's branch, so it waits for it. `repo` is left out when the reader
may not read the repo.

An agent block attached to the row (`attachment`) was closed, and
another may have taken its place: it no longer counts toward Doing.

The row is in Doing, every block of it that isn't closed has been
idle for longer than the project's `stall_minutes`, and no PR is on
it (Arugula #404). `since` is when the last of them went idle, in
milliseconds. It names no block: who holds the row is the block's
chip, for a reader who may see it.

The row's item is blocked by an open item (a `blocks` edge, Arugula
#403): the row stays in its lane. `number`, `title` and `repo` are
left out when the reader may not read the blocker (one such mark
stands for all of them: "something you can't see").

board.description:
The other board the blocker is a row of, when the reader may read
the blocker and it is on a board other than this one.

lead.description: The session that leads that board, when one does.

oneOf.description:
The row's item is in a loop of open ordering edges (Plane can make
one): it shares its `step` with the others in the loop.

MovedFrom.description: Where a Doc a machine moved to a team was (Arugula #863).

doc.description: The Doc's id in that machine's library (16 hex digits).

machine.description: The machine's id in control: the one that signs the call.

moved_from.description:
A machine moving one of its Docs here (Arugula #863), over
[`AGENT_PROJECT_DOCS`]: kept as the Doc's [`Doc::moved_from`]. Its
`machine` must be the one signing; a person never sends it.

session.description:
The name of the agent session that made it (#1258), over
[`AGENT_PROJECT_DOCS`]: kept as its [`Doc::agent`]'s `session`, so a
comment on the Doc can mention that session. A person's is ignored.

NewSection.description:
A new Doc's section: a heading, and its Markdown now or an intent for
later.

Operation.description: What a deploy applies, as approved.

planned.description: The hash of the deploy's `planned` event, hex.

source_ref.description: The commit's sha or the artifact's digest.

PasskeyAssertion.description: A passkey's assertion as the hub checked it (M218): each base64url.

PlanStep.description: Which of a deploy plan run's two tokens a box asks for (#1985).

oneOf.description:
A GitHub token that reads the deploy's repository, to fetch the
commit: nothing of the commit's has run yet.

A GitHub token that writes the repository's contents, to push
chant's ledger: everything the plan ran is stopped by then, the box's
daemon checked what the plan added, and the token reaches only the
daemon's own push, never the run user.

Pointer.description:
What a row points at. `None` is free text. The ids are the platform's:
`fi_…` (a mirrored PR or issue), `iss_…`, `run_…`, `hw_…`, `pdc_…` (a
project Doc).

oneOf.description: An agent block on a machine.

pane.description: The block's pane, as `%N` or `N`; stored as `N`.

oneOf.description:
An `https://` URL, as evidence (a CI page, a report). The platform
takes only `https`, no userinfo, at most [`LINK_MAX`] bytes.

A project Doc (`pdc_…`) of the board's own project. Only a Doc strip
or a `reference` attachment carries one.

A Doc block on a machine. `title` is a snapshot from when it was
linked, since the machine may be off; a [`BoardDoc`] reads the
machine's copy instead when the copy sits in the board's project.

PrUntil.description: What a watch on a pull request waits for.

oneOf.description: It merged.
It closed, merged or not.
No check on its head commit is queued or running (Arugula #1033).

A check on its head commit failed: once, however often it flips. A
merge-group run's failure counts for a queued PR.
It left the merge queue without merging.
Its checks passed and GitHub says it can merge cleanly.

ProjectGrant.description:
A project owner saying the platform may start and instruct runs on
`project`'s hosted workspaces, under `delegation`.

account.description: v2: the granting owner's account, in the bytes. Empty in v1.

by.description: v1: the signing device. Empty in v2, which no device signs.

expires.description: When it stops counting (ms); `None`: never (v1 only).

owner.description: `team:<id>` or `account:<id>`, as the granter saw it.

passkey.description:
v2: the passkey's assertion over [`ProjectGrant::passkey_challenge`],
its signature. Kept beside the bytes, not in them.

sig.description:
v1: its Ed25519 signature over [`ProjectGrant::body`], hex. Empty
in v2.

v.description:
Its format, [`V1`] or [`V2`]: absent is v1 (every grant from before
DK6).

Proof.description:
The mark on a Done row that is proven. A Done row without one is not
proven yet.

pointer.description: What proves it: the merged PR, or the evidence attached.

ProofBy.description: How a Done row is proven.

oneOf.description:
A PR of the row merged with every check on its head completed and
none red.
A `proof` attachment.

Proposal.description:
What an agent session asks its asker to approve (Arugula #1278): it
does nothing itself. The proposal is an ask in their staff room
(`via` `ask:prp_…`) that mentions them, so it's under Needs you and
pushed to their phone; **Approve** does it as them, through the same
path their own press would take, and **Deny** drops it. Either way
`ask.answered` tells the session. Chat never approves it.

oneOf.description:
An agent session on one of the project's native issues, as
**Agent on this** starts one: on the box the project's pool picks,
in `repo` when it's given, told `prompt` (by default, to work on
the issue).

Stop these sessions of the project (`ses_…`), as their cards'
**Stop** does. A machine's agent (Arugula #1417) names agent blocks
on its own machine instead (`blocks`, by pane), and no sessions.

"Run this board" (Arugula #1416): start the board's lead on
`machine`, and grant it issue agents on that machine and `machines`,
`cap` at once, until the board closes or `lapse_days` pass. Approve
writes the board's grant (replacing any it had) and starts the lead
there. A machine's agent's only: `machine` is a machine of its
person's, by name or id (none: the asking machine).

prompt.description: What the lead is told; none: to run the board.

oneOf.description:
A to-do (Arugula #1462): work its person does outside Arugula (an
approval on GitHub, a script with their credentials, a secret put
somewhere) and reports back on. Its card's choices are [`TODO_DONE`]
and [`TODO_CANT`], with a note; nothing is done on Approve, and the
agent may cancel it. `what`, `why` and `how` are plain text, shown
as written (no Markdown): `what` one line, `how` the steps,
commands verbatim. It's for the person the agent works for (a
session's asker, a machine's owner): the agent doesn't name them.

conversation.description: A machine's agent's conversation, which the answer is for.

issue.description: Its card: one of the project's native issues, by number.

PublicLink.description:
A team Doc's public link (Arugula #871). The platform keeps its key with
the Doc, and gives it only to those who read the Doc; control holds the
ciphertext and never the key. The URL is `<viewer>/<id>#k=<key>`, the
viewer being `/control.json`'s `doc_viewer`.

behind.description: The Doc changed since the served version was sealed.

id.description: The link's id at control: 32 lower-case hex digits.

key.description: The link's key, base64url without padding: 32 bytes.

updated_at.description: When the served version was made (ms); 0 while there is none.

url.description:
The address anyone can open, `<viewer>/<id>#k=<key>`; empty when this
control keeps no shared Docs, or from an older platform. The platform
page can't read `/control.json` (the platform's host answers none of
the hub's), so the platform says where the viewer is.

ver.description: The version control serves; 0 while the first one isn't uploaded.

PushAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_PUSH`]'s body: which session, and the ref it pushes,
which must be the session's own branch exactly.

clone.description:
A token to clone the session's repo instead, with `contents: read`
alone: a repo linked to the project that no box's setup cloned is
cloned at the session's start, shallow (Fleet 6). The same checks
as a push's. An older platform ignores it and mints a push's.

oneOf.description:
An installation token for the session's repo alone, with
`contents: write` and never `workflows` (aru-115, amended), or
`contents: read` for a clone, minted for this push or clone: the box hands it to git in one process's environment, never
to a file, then revokes it at `revoke` (`DELETE`, the token as its
bearer). `expires_at` is GitHub's.
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

ReadyRun.description: A run that's ready for this machine and hasn't started.

deploy.description:
A deploy's run (M219): the deploy it applies, with its owner's
approval, which the machine checks itself before it starts.

deploy_plan.description:
A chant→Fly deploy's plan run (#1985): the deploy whose plan it
runs, before anyone approves it. A machine from before it reads
neither this nor [`ReadyRun::deploy`], and a deploy's box refuses
that.

grant.description:
The project's standing grant the run starts under (M211), when it's
`pending` under one, and the project's revokes the platform holds.
The machine checks them against its own enrollment before anything
starts, and keeps the revokes.

last_seq.description: The run's latest event: the machine's first report is the next.

op.description: The S37 operation's bytes (`arugula op v1`), exactly as stored.

op_hash.description: Their SHA-256, hex: the machine checks the bytes against it.

passkey_log.description:
A v2 grant's granter's passkey log, as the platform read it from the
hub (DK6, as `crate::runs::RunStart::passkey_log`): the machine takes
only its removals.

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) the machine is.

RelationDirection.description: Which end of an edge a row's item is.

oneOf.description: The row's item is the first end: it blocks, duplicates, was found from.
The row's item is the second end: it is blocked by the other.

RelationKind.description:
What an edge between two work items says (Arugula #403). Only `blocks`
gates: it keeps the blocked item's row out of the ready set until the
blocker is closed. `before` (#761) says an order and gates nothing; it
can't close a cycle with `blocks` edges.

oneOf.description: The first item blocks the second.
The first item duplicates the second.
The first item was found while working on the second.

The first item comes before the second, in the order the work is
done in.

RelationSource.description:
Who made an edge. `plane` and `github` edges are read from there, and
Arugula doesn't change them.

Report.description: One state change, signed by the machine that made it.

detail.description:
A JSON object's text, exactly as signed: an exit code (`exit`), a
pane (`pane`, `epoch`), or why it failed (`reason`).

seq.description: The event's number in the run.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula run event v1`, hex.

oneOf.description: Kept: the run moved.

Kept before: the same event, signed the same (a retry whose answer
was lost).

Not kept, and sending it again won't change that. `now` is the run's
state when it moved on without this machine (canceled, say), and
`next` the event number it's at when this one's isn't it.

RollBack.description:
What a roll back goes back to: an earlier deploy of the same
environment that succeeded, and what its log kept of what it ran (for
chant→Fly: [`IMAGE`], and chant's release record, [`CHANT_COMPONENT`],
[`CHANT_ENV`] and [`CHANT_DIGEST`]).

agent.description:
The machine whose agent added the row, if one did (it may remove
it; nobody else's agent may).

ask.description: The row's one open question: asked, else raised by the board.

asked.description: The last [`ASKED_SHOWN`] asks answered, newest first.

attachments.description: Work and proof attached to the row, oldest first.

block.description:
A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it, when that
machine holds `boards.write` over the board's project.

docs.description:
The Docs linked to the row (#517): its spike or research, in order.
They move no lane and prove nothing.

group.description: The group (`zon_…`) the row belongs to, if any.

held.description:
The session that holds the row's issue (Arugula #765), if one does.
Never set on a row whose issue is closed.

lane.description: Where the row is, from the live state of its items.

lane_set.description:
Never sent: a row's lane follows its work, and nobody sets it
(Arugula #1383). Deprecated with [`BOARD_ROW_LANE`]; a client from
0.70.128 doesn't read it.

live.description:
A `fi_`, `iss_` or `run_` pointer's state now, when the reader may see the
item ([`BoardView`] is read with it; a write's answer has it too).

marks.description:
What the lane doesn't say, in a fixed order: `not_finished`,
`cancelled`, `after`, `blocked_by`, then one `earlier` for each closed block.

place.description:
The column the row sits in on the Steps chart (Arugula #824): the
same longest-path layout as [`Row::step`], but over every row with an
issue or a PR, done ones included, using their ordering edges whether
the other end is open or closed. So finishing work never moves a row.
Absent for a row with no issue or PR.

proof.description: Set only on a Done row that is proven.

relations.description: The edges of the row's item, both ways, for the drawer.

sessions.description:
The agent sessions started on the row's issue, oldest first
(Arugula #843). A live one puts the row in Doing.

status.description:
Kept for old clients: `needs_input` when the row has an open ask
(#367), `none` otherwise. Nothing writes it.

step.description:
Where the row falls in the board's order (Arugula #762): 1 plus the
highest step of the open rows that come before it, worked out on
every read and never stored. Absent for a row with no issue or PR,
and for a Done row. Doing and Review rows are step 1.

RowRelation.description: An edge of a row's item, as the reader sees it.

item.description: The `iss_` or `fi_` id of the item at the other end, with `other`.

other.description:
The item at the other end. Left out when the reader may not read it:
the edge is "something you can't see", with no title or number.

removable.description: The reader may take it off: an owner or editor, and it was made here.

RowSession.description: An agent session started on a row's issue (Arugula #843).

branch.description: The one ref it may push, `arugula/<8 hex>-<slug>`.

live.description:
Whether it moves the row: it is under way, or done with its PR not
yet sent. A session that isn't live is shown dimmed.

pr.description: Its PR's link, once its asker sent it.

state.description:
Its state as the platform keeps it: `queued`, `working`,
`needs_input`, `done`, `failed`, `unresponsive` or `stopped`.

Running.description: What happens to runs already going when a grant is revoked.

oneOf.description: They finish.
They're stopped too.

Secret.description:
One secret, by its name as an environment variable. Its value is never
printed (`Debug` leaves it out).

revoke.description:
A short-lived token's revoke URL (`DELETE`, the token as its bearer):
the box revokes it when its driver ends (M219).

plan_step.description:
A deploy's plan run (#1985) asks twice, a token each time: to fetch
its source, before anything of the commit's runs, and to push
chant's ledger, after everything that ran is stopped. Any other
run asks once, with none.

oneOf.description:
The environment's secrets and the driver's short-lived tokens, by
name. Given once per run.
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

Section.description: One section: pending (`body` null) until it's written.

body.description: Its Markdown (the machine Doc's: `chart` and `svg` fences draw).

id.description: The Doc's own: `s1`, `s2`, … in the order they were added.

intent.description: One line on what it will hold, shown while it's pending.

rev.description: Counts the writes to its body.

SessionAction.description:
Something a person asked of a session that only its box can do: answer
its open question, approve or deny its open permission, or cancel the
turn under way (the session goes on). Stopping the session isn't one:
control moves it to `stopped`, and it leaves the work list.

by_name.description:
Its login (or the name the platform has for it), for the
transcript's "Answered by" note: empty from a platform that doesn't
send it.

id.description: `sac_` and 32 hex characters: the box does each once.

request.description:
The open request it answers ([`SessionDetail::request`]); `None`:
whichever is open.

SessionDetail.description:
A [`SessionReport`]'s detail: each kind fills its own fields (the
module's docs say which), and leaves the rest out.

actions.description:
The actions ([`SessionAction`]) this report carries out: `answer`,
`approve` and `deny` on the `needs_input` to `working` report;
`cancel` on the turn's `working` to `done`, or a heartbeat when no
turn was under way.

block.description:
The agent block the session runs in, on taking it, and on a parked
one's next turn, which runs in a block opened again (Arugula #215).

by.description: An `in_block` turn's: who typed its prompt, when the block says.

commits.description:
A turn's: `"SHA subject"` for each commit it made, newest first, as
the daemon's turn work has them (`arugula_proto::api::Work`).

diffstat.description:
A turn's: `git diff --stat` from its start to HEAD, shortened as the
daemon's turn work shortens it.

finish.description:
A turn's: what its finish step did (M261), when the workspace has
one. A failed one isn't pushed.

harness.description:
Taking a session (M264): the agent the box runs it on, which is
`claude` when the one asked for isn't on the box.

head.description: A turn's: HEAD after it, abbreviated.

in_block.description:
A turn's start that came from the session's agent block itself, not
from the thread's prompts: someone typed in the block (its Open
button), or the agent woke itself. It names no prompts.

model.description:
The model its agent runs on (Arugula #215), as the agent names it
(`Opus 5.5`), once the box knows it and whenever it changes; each
turn's report says it again. At most [`MODEL_MAX`] bytes.

options.description:
To `needs_input` for a permission: its option ids; for a question,
its first question's choices, by their labels (Arugula #214).

prompts.description: The queued prompts a turn starts with (`spr_…`).

pushed.description: A turn's: whether it pushed the branch (HEAD is on the remote).

reply.description:
A turn's: the agent's last message, at most [`REPLY_MAX`] bytes
(less when the rest of the detail needs the room). The platform
posts it in the session's thread: a review's as the review (M264),
any other's as the turn's answer. A box from before every turn sent
it sends it for reviews only.

typed.description:
An `in_block` turn's: the start of the prompt typed there, at most
[`TYPED_MAX`] characters; none when the agent woke itself. The
platform says it in the session's thread, as its own line (Arugula
#215), and it's never a prompt.

uncommitted.description: A turn's: how many paths it left uncommitted.

SessionHold.description:
The session that holds an issue's row (Arugula #765): the one that last
started an agent on it, or took it. It is the issue's, so a row on two
boards shows the same holder, and it lasts until the issue closes or the
session lets it go. The same shape as [`BoardLead`].

at.description: When the session took the row.

machine_name.description: The machine's name now; empty while it can't be told.

session.description: The session's name, as its machine's daemon matches it.

SessionIssuesAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_ISSUES`]'s body: which session asks, and what. The
project is never named: it is the session's, and the platform finds it.

oneOf.description: A page of the project's issues, newest first.

One issue by its number in the project: it, its timeline and its
newest comments.

A comment on one, as the session's asker, labelled as posted by the
session.

A new issue, with the asker's rights, opened as the session's own;
its labels from those the project's issues already have.

A new Doc in the project, with the asker's rights, as the session's
own.
A write to one of the project's Docs that this session made.
One of the project's Docs, or with no `id` the list of them.

A room's messages, as the session's asker may read them (Arugula
#1276): `room` is `staff` (the asker's staff room in the project) or
a room of the project (a board's or an issue's thread, a channel).
Oldest first, after `after`, or the newest page; with `thread`, the
replies under that message.

A post in such a room as the asker's agent, labelled with the
session: under `parent` when given. It reaches whom an agent's post
there reaches: a board's lead, the person in their staff room, an
agent it names.

The project's boards, as the session's asker may read them (Arugula
#1381); with `board` (`brd_…`, or an open board's exact title) that
one board, with its lead, its rows and who works each.

A proposal for the session's asker to approve or deny (Arugula
#1278): a card in their staff room, under Needs you and on their
phone. The session does nothing itself: the person's Approve does
it, as them, and `ask.answered` tells the session how it went.

Cancel one of the session's own to-dos (Arugula #1462) while it's
open: it leaves its person's Needs you, and `ask.answered` says
`cancelled`. Only a to-do is cancelled.

comments.description: Oldest first: the newest of its thread.

comments_in_chat.description:
The comments were left out: they're in chat, which is off for
the session's asker (Arugula #746). Absent when they're there.

more_comments.description: There are older comments than these.

oneOf.description: Posted, as this message of the issue's thread.
Opened: the issue, and its page's link.
A Doc, as made, written or read, and its page's link.
The project's Docs.

A room's messages (`ThreadRead`): its id, oldest first, and the seq
to read on after.
Posted (`ThreadPost`), as this message of the room.
The project's boards (`BoardRead` with no board).
One board (`BoardRead` with a board).

Proposed (`Propose`): its id (`prp_…`, what `ask.answered`
matches as `ask`), and its card's message in the staff room.
Cancelled (`ProposalCancel`).
Not done, and why (the agent reads it).

SessionIssuesOp.description:
What a session's agent does in its project: read, comment on and open
its native issues, make, write and read its Docs (aru-118), and read and
post in its rooms as its asker's agent (Arugula #1276), and read its
boards (Arugula #1381), nothing else. The route kept its first name,
`session/issues`, for the boxes already calling it.

oneOf.description: A page of the project's issues, newest first.

One issue by its number in the project: it, its timeline and its
newest comments.

A comment on one, as the session's asker, labelled as posted by the
session.

A new issue, with the asker's rights, opened as the session's own;
its labels from those the project's issues already have.

A new Doc in the project, with the asker's rights, as the session's
own.
A write to one of the project's Docs that this session made.
One of the project's Docs, or with no `id` the list of them.

A room's messages, as the session's asker may read them (Arugula
#1276): `room` is `staff` (the asker's staff room in the project) or
a room of the project (a board's or an issue's thread, a channel).
Oldest first, after `after`, or the newest page; with `thread`, the
replies under that message.

A post in such a room as the asker's agent, labelled with the
session: under `parent` when given. It reaches whom an agent's post
there reaches: a board's lead, the person in their staff room, an
agent it names.

The project's boards, as the session's asker may read them (Arugula
#1381); with `board` (`brd_…`, or an open board's exact title) that
one board, with its lead, its rows and who works each.

A proposal for the session's asker to approve or deny (Arugula
#1278): a card in their staff room, under Needs you and on their
phone. The session does nothing itself: the person's Approve does
it, as them, and `ask.answered` tells the session how it went.

Cancel one of the session's own to-dos (Arugula #1462) while it's
open: it leaves its person's Needs you, and `ask.answered` says
`cancelled`. Only a to-do is cancelled.

SessionPrompt.description: A prompt queued in a session's thread.

author_name.description:
The author's login (or the name the platform has for them), for the
transcript's "from" note: empty from a platform that doesn't send
it, and for GitHub's text, whose login is in `author`.

source.description:
`member` (a project member's, in the thread), `github` (text from
GitHub: a PR's review, a check's log) or `arugula` (Arugula's own
word to the session: a watch it made fired or ended, Arugula #1035).

SessionReport.description:
What a machine says of one of its sessions, signed: its fields are
`arugula_e2e::session::Event`'s.

detail.description: A JSON object's text ([`SessionDetail`]), exactly as signed.

n.description: The machine's report number in the session, from 1.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula session event v1`, hex.

SessionWatchAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_WATCH`]'s body: which session asks, and what. The watch
is the session's own, and its asker's: a session sees and cancels no
other's.

oneOf.description: Wake this session when any of `targets` gets there.

event.description:
An event target too, as [`crate::watch::WatchCreate::event`]'s:
left out when none, so a watch without one reads as before. A
`#N` in its match is the session's project's.

match.description: With `event`: the type's match fields an event must equal.

note.description:
With `event`: why the agent watches, handed back when it fires;
at most [`crate::watch::NOTE_MAX`] characters.

oneOf.description: Its live watches.
One of them by id, or all.

Its project's events after `after` (Arugula #1273), as
[`crate::events::AGENT_EVENTS`] reads a machine's: those its asker
may read, answered [`SessionWatchGiven::Events`].

limit.description:
At most this many: [`crate::events::READ_LIMIT_DEFAULT`] when
none.

types.description:
Only these types ([`crate::events::read_types`]). Empty: every
type.

SessionWatchOp.description: What a session's agent does with its watches.

oneOf.description: Wake this session when any of `targets` gets there.

event.description:
An event target too, as [`crate::watch::WatchCreate::event`]'s:
left out when none, so a watch without one reads as before. A
`#N` in its match is the session's project's.

match.description: With `event`: the type's match fields an event must equal.

note.description:
With `event`: why the agent watches, handed back when it fires;
at most [`crate::watch::NOTE_MAX`] characters.

oneOf.description: Its live watches.
One of them by id, or all.

Its project's events after `after` (Arugula #1273), as
[`crate::events::AGENT_EVENTS`] reads a machine's: those its asker

limit.description:
At most this many: [`crate::events::READ_LIMIT_DEFAULT`] when

types.description:
Only these types ([`crate::events::read_types`]). Empty: every

Status.description: Where a row stands. `None` says nothing.

TodoConversation.description:
The conversation a machine's agent's to-do is for (Arugula #1462): its
harness and its id there, so an answer can find it again once its block
is gone. The machine is the one that asked. Any card's or board ask's
answer wakes it (Arugula #1465): [`MachinePropose::conversation`],
`boards::NewAsk::conversation`.

WatchCancelled.description:
What [`WatchCancel`] cancelled, by id. The session that asked is told
by this answer, and gets no message for them.

WatchList.description: The machine's live watches, the newest first.

expires_ms.description: When it expires, in ms since the epoch.

met.description:
What happened already, for [`WatchState::AlreadyMet`]: ids and
states only ("arugula-salad/arugula#2095 merged by aaron at …").

WatchRow.description: One watch, as a list shows it.

every_ms.description:
A standing watch's gap (Arugula #1280), in milliseconds; none for one
that fires once.

session.description: The Claude Code session it wakes.

targets.description:
Each target in words ("arugula-salad/arugula#2095 until merged"), so
a reader that doesn't know a newer kind still shows it.

oneOf.description: Waiting.

What it waits for had already happened when it was asked: no watch
was made.
It happened, and the session was told.
Its time ran out.

It can't fire any more: a target can't be read now, or the session
is gone.
A state this side doesn't know yet.

WatchTarget.description: What a watch waits for: one of these happening fires it.

oneOf.description:
A pull request on github.com, in a repo linked through Arugula's
GitHub App.

A hosted agent session (`ses_…`, Arugula #1034), until it settles as
`wait` with `agent_session` says: done with nothing queued, waiting
for input, failed or stopped.

A reply in a chat thread: a message in `room` under `parent` (its
root's number), or any message in the room without one, that the
session that made the watch didn't write. With `from`, only one by
that person (their login or name, any case).
A run (`run_…`) or a deploy (`dep_…`), until it ends however it ends.

revokes.description:
Every revoke of the project's grants the platform holds, on every
pull, ready runs or not: a machine checks them against the grants
its runs going were started under, and stops those a `running stop`
covers, and against its sessions' grants, ending those any revoke
covers (a turn under way finishes first, unless it says `running
stop`).

sessions.description:
The sessions on this machine's workspace that haven't ended, for a
machine that takes them ([`TAKES_SESSION`]).

ZoneKind.description:
A zone's kind: every zone a read answers is a `lane`, one of the four
([`Lane`]). No one makes a zone.
